travel_dk.h: The famous claim that happiness stops rising at $75,000 came from a 2010 study by two Nobel laureates. Later analysis revealed something subtler: its measure was better at detecting the disappearance of unhappiness than increases in happiness. Newer data suggest happiness keeps rising with income for most people—even above $100,000—while the plateau mainly appears among the least-happy minority.
